title: EPA Relaxes Coal Ash Monitoring and Closure Requirements in 2018
description_short: On July 18, 2018, EPA finalized coal-ash amendments allowing conditional monitoring exemptions and giving some disposal units more time to close.
description_medium: On July 18, 2018, EPA finalized amendments to its 2015 coal-ash disposal regulations. The changes allowed permitting authorities to suspend groundwater monitoring where evidence showed no potential for hazardous constituents to reach the uppermost aquifer. They also changed groundwater protection standards and gave certain units triggered into closure additional time to stop accepting waste. EPA presented the amendments as added flexibility for states and utilities.
description_long: On July 18, 2018, the Environmental Protection Agency finalized its first amendments to the 2015 federal regulations governing coal ash from electric utilities and independent power producers. The changes affected requirements for coal-ash landfills and surface impoundments, including groundwater monitoring and the timing of closure. Under one alternative performance standard, an approved state permitting authority, or EPA where it issued permits, could suspend groundwater monitoring if evidence demonstrated no potential for hazardous constituents to migrate to the uppermost aquifer during operation and post-closure care. Another permitted technical certifications instead of certification by a professional engineer. EPA also revised groundwater protection standards for constituents without established federal drinking-water limits. The rule provided additional time to stop receiving waste and initiate closure for certain units, including unlined impoundments with elevated groundwater contamination and units failing the aquifer location restriction. Acting Administrator Andrew Wheeler described the action as giving states and utilities more flexibility. These regulatory changes identify the requirements relaxed; they do not establish a measured change in contamination at any particular facility or waterway.

proposal.description_long: On July 29, 2020, the Environmental Protection Agency finalized revisions to federal regulations governing coal-combustion residuals, or coal ash, from electric utilities. EPA said the rule implemented court decisions that had vacated certain closure requirements and added provisions to improve public access to information about coal-ash management. The agency’s fact sheet characterized the action as targeted revisions that kept the major protections and requirements of the 2015 rule in place while addressing litigation, statutory changes and implementation experience. This supports a specific account of a regulatory amendment, not an unqualified claim that all coal-ash safeguards were weakened. The original EPA news-release URL now returns 404, while the attached AP and NPR URLs are general news pages rather than reporting on this rule. EPA’s surviving release and fact sheet identify the action and its stated scope, but the packet contains no facility-level records or monitoring data showing what changed at a particular site or whether nearby water quality was affected. Those outcomes should not be asserted without separate evidence.

proposal.description_long: In 2018, National Security Adviser John Bolton reorganized the National Security Council, eliminating its standalone Global Health Security directorate. The Los Angeles Times’ later account of the pandemic response attributes the decision to Bolton. TIME’s contemporaneous reporting says the team was disbanded as part of a broader NSC restructuring and quotes an administration official saying related responsibilities were absorbed into another directorate. The available sources therefore support describing the loss of a dedicated global-health office and a change in organizational structure. They do not establish that every outbreak-monitoring or preparedness function disappeared, identify a complete list of affected staff and reassigned duties, or prove that the reorganization caused a particular later operational failure. The TIME link supplied in this record now returns 404, and the AP hub link does not contain event-specific documentation; accessible contemporaneous reporting is useful supplementary evidence but should be added to the record’s source list through the normal evidence update process. A careful account should distinguish the structural decision from contested claims about its consequences.
proposal.description_medium: Contemporaneous reporting says John Bolton’s 2018 NSC reorganization eliminated its standalone Global Health Security directorate.
